reading.text:
Reading for def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.IsBrownianFiltration (locked before any Lean is shown).

Paper notion (sec 2): W is a Brownian motion WITH RESPECT TO the filtration (F_t): the filtration
is the usual augmentation of the one generated by W, N and F_0 (W, N, F_0 independent), so W is
an (F_t)-Brownian motion: 
 (a) W is (F_t)-adapted (W_t is F_t-measurable);
 (b) for s <= t, the increment W_t - W_s is independent of F_s
 (with (a),(b) and the BM law, W is an (F_t)-martingale with quadratic variation t I_d - what the
 Ito integral / PRP / BDG need).
A faithful Lean predicate IsBrownianFiltration F W must contain (a) and (b) (or an equivalent:
"W_{t+s}-W_s independent of F_s"). It need not encode "F is generated by W, N, F_0" (that is
part of the setting rather than of the predicate name) - if the predicate claims to be the
paper's filtration hypothesis but omits generation, note it, since the PRP fails for a larger
filtration. A weaker predicate (adaptedness only) is NOT the paper's notion (the Ito isometry and
martingale property would fail).

comparison.text:
Comparison for def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.IsBrownianFiltration.

Lean (LevyStochCalc/Brownian/Filtered.lean): structure IsBrownianFiltration (W : BrownianMotion P) F
with
  measurable : forall t, W_t is F_t-measurable          (my (a), adaptedness);
  indep_future : forall s >= 0, F_s is independent of sup_{t > s} sigma(W_t - W_s)  (my (b), in the
  stronger joint form: the whole future increment sigma-algebra, not each increment separately).
This is the standard definition of an (F_t)-Brownian motion (with the BM law from the structure);
it gives the martingale property and quadratic variation the Ito integral, BDG and the PRP need.
It does not encode "F generated by W, N, F_0" - as anticipated in my reading, that belongs to the
setting (the consumers instantiate F with the augmented joint filtration enlJoint).
Adaptedness is asked for every real t (including t < 0), satisfiable for the R-indexed filtrations
used (natural filtrations contain sigma(W_t)).
Note (not a defect of this definition): the predicate is scalar; PaperSolution asks it of each
component D.W.W j separately. Componentwise independence from F_s is weaker than independence of
the vector increment from F_s, but the consumers take F = enlJoint, the augmentation of the joint
natural filtration of the independent driver, for which the joint property holds.
Verdict: faithful.

author_review.disagreements:
No substantive disagreement. The review shown records "faithful with representation choices": the
R-indexed adaptedness, joint independence of the future increments, and use per component. I
recorded "faithful". Joint independence of all future increments from F_s is the standard
definition of an (F_t)-Brownian motion, not a choice. That the predicate is applied to each
component separately (rather than to the vector increment) is a property of its consumers. I noted
it, and it is harmless there because they take the joint augmented filtration enlJoint. The
difference is only in the label.
